Section 2 pins <security_key> to AMGT-s-12's identity layer (Bloomberg ticker, spaces->underscores) and states it is the SAME string across all three prefixes for one security, with an explicit note that a vendor's own id (sa_id, CIK, CUSIP) is never used as the key. Section 3 pins the stamp to UTC-at-write-start (not the vendor as_of), mirrors the OPAL_ASSETS run_date-vs-as_of lesson, and states a multi-stage run mints >=1 stamp per stage -- directly answering AMGT-s-14's own 'a single refresh under one timestamp is a violation' bar. Section 4 states the two load-bearing rules the order named (never write to an existing path; versioning is the safety net, not the mechanism; a consumer reads the lexicographically-greatest stamp under a prefix, computable from list-objects-v2 --delimiter / CommonPrefixes with no index or pointer file). Section 5 is the part the order's item (b) did not explicitly ask for but AC7 grades: it states source/last-run/outcome/re-run-alone concretely for AMGT-s-14 -- source = the vendor/engine segment; last run = the max stamp under a prefix (already defined in section 4); outcome = a `_outcome.json` sibling key at the SAME stamp, written even on failure, so a failed run is never a silently-missing stamp indistinguishable from 'never ran'; re-run alone = structural, because every class lives under a disjoint vendor/engine segment and rule 1 forbids overwriting an existing stamp, so a re-run of one class cannot touch another class's keys by construction. Section 6 states what is deliberately NOT built (no lifecycle/replication/notification/IAM/second bucket), tying back to this cell's own BOUNDS (G-19, G-20, NO IAM CHANGE) so a reader does not mistake an absence for an oversight.
